title.value: Neural correlates of local parallelism during naturalistic vision
title.justification: The paper primarily focuses on exploring the neural mechanisms associated with the perception of local parallelism and its role in scene perception.
title.quote: Neural correlates of local parallelism during naturalistic vision

extractions.description: This study investigates the neural mechanisms involved in the perception of local parallelism during naturalistic vision using fMRI. By employing an image-computable algorithm, the authors analyzed the impact of local symmetry on brain activity in visual areas while participants viewed manipulated scenes. Results highlighted significant neural signals related to parallelism in various brain regions such as V1-V4, PPA, and RSC, suggesting a pivotal role of parallelism in scene perception and visual processing hierarchy.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on neural mechanisms and visual perception, rather than any specific issues related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We here uncover the neural mechanisms of one important perceptual grouping cue, local parallelism.

primary_category.justification: The main focus of the paper is on neural correlates and visual perception mechanisms rather than sustainability or development themes related to climate or ecology.
primary_category.quote: This study investigates the neural mechanisms involved in the perception of local parallelism during naturalistic vision.

secondary_categories.quote: Studying perceptual organization in real-world scenes, however, requires image-computable algorithms for detecting grouping cues in such complex images.

primary_sub_category.justification: The study does not align with any sub-categories under Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, as it is centered on visual neuroscience and perceptual studies.
primary_sub_category.quote: In this experiment, we investigate the effect of local parallelism on the neural representations of scene categories in several visually active brain regions.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no additional secondary sub-categories that could be suitable, given the paper’s focus on the brain’s visual processing of parallelism.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We address the first question in our second experiment. We explored which brain regions carry a signature of local parallelism by harnessing the natural variability in a large database of natural scenes.

new_primary_category.quote: Our study clearly shows that signals of local parallelism are present throughout the visual processing hierarchy, presumably originating in area V4.
